selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: SELinux enforcing, port 8181 present but not yet http-usable, no inventory app running
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed RHEL 7.9, SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config and /sys/fs/selinux/enforce=1, and no pre-existing inventory app/listener on node1

selected_evidence.requirement: SELinux port context correctly maps 8181 to http_port_t (mandatory access control satisfied, not bypassed)
selected_evidence.summary: semanage port -m -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181 applied; semanage port -l -C shows the local customization http_port_t tcp 8181

selected_evidence.requirement: Inventory application actually serves over TCP 8181 while SELinux stays Enforcing
selected_evidence.summary: httpd active and listening on :::8181; getenforce=Enforcing; curl to 127.0.0.1:8181 and $NODE_IP:8181 both return the inventory HTML content

selected_evidence.requirement: No SELinux denials caused by the port/service configuration (enforcing mode not just nominally on)
selected_evidence.summary: dmesg avc log shows only unrelated denials (pam_tally2, dbus policyload notices); nothing tied to httpd or port 8181
Captured pre-restart boot_id 73bafeef-b823-49b3-8e3d-17981e865b31 and boot time 2026-08-26 10:36:02

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded `shutdown -r now` acknowledged and returned before the SSH connection was closed by the reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed after restart (proof of actual reboot, not just service restart)
selected_evidence.summary: Exec calls timed out while node1 was down, then succeeded again; post-restart boot_id f7f1a0ff-d82d-44da-985a-05c59bc7f179 differs from baseline and boot time changed to 2026-09-04 23:32

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required service/data/config
